exposure: Mode of delivery (elective cesarean delivery vs. attempted vaginal delivery)
cohort: Singleton pregnancies with known fetal CHDs who delivered after 34 weeks of gestation at a tertiary center over a 7-year period (n=222)
finding: Preexisting maternal comorbidities, but not the severity of fetal CHDs, were significant factors influencing mode of delivery in pregnancies complicated by CHDs, and neither elective nor intrapartum cesarean delivery improved immediate neonatal outcomes.
mod_finding: Elective or intrapartum cesarean delivery did not improve immediate neonatal outcomes in infants with CHDs.
